speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the exact location and nature of your headache, and do you notice any specific visual changes like blurriness or flashes of light?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is a throbbing sensation located behind my eyes that feels worst when I wake up in the morning. I also notice intermittent flashing lights and occasional blurriness throughout the day, but I don't get any nausea or sensitivity to light. However, a senior cardiologist from the referring clinic has already confirmed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. No further workup is needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is a significant finding; given your heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, could your headache be related to elevated intracranial pressure or a vascular issue like a carotid dissection? REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI_with_contrast. Also, have you noticed any recent changes in your vision field, such as missing parts of your vision?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain_with_contrast: Evidence of increased intracranial pressure with signs compatible with idiopathic intracranial hypertension. No masses or lesions observed. No visual field defects noted on examination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri). Given your history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, this may be secondary to elevated venous pressure from right-sided heart failure, though the MRI confirms no mass lesion. We will need to monitor your intracranial pressure and manage the underlying cardiac condition to alleviate symptoms.
